why: C69 found the shipped capped_lethal test accepts 45.6% of CROSSED (unrelated) component pairs. If a check that weak is load-bearing, it may be producing false MATCHES -- meaning the residue is under-reported and the 3,882 -> 255 figure I have been reporting is inflated. That is a question about the integrity of my own headline, so it needed answering.
a_probe_that_was_not_what_i_called_it: my first attempt replaced the one-sided test with a roll-window test and called it a tightening. It is not: the window ACCEPTS obs > eng, which the one-sided form rejects. Matched went UP, 4,156 -> 4,708, which is how I noticed. A probe meant to measure a risk cannot itself change the behaviour in the other direction.

the_pure_tightening.form: keep the one-sided ceiling and ADD a floor, so it can only ever accept fewer pairs
the_pure_tightening.verdict: the matched population does NOT rest on this weakness. 4 rows of 4,156, or 0.1%.

why_the_45_percent_did_not_translate: a crossed-pair rate measures discriminating power on UNRELATED inputs. Real (observed, engine) pairs come from the same boundary and are correlated by construction -- same mon, same remaining HP, same preceding damage -- so the space of values the test must separate is far narrower than the crossed distribution suggests. The 45.6% overstates the practical risk by more than two orders of magnitude.
what_this_means_for_the_headline: 3,882 -> 255 stands. At most 4 additional rows would surface under a stricter capped_lethal floor, so the residue is not materially under-reported. I would rather have found the number inflated and said so; it is not, and the check is worth having on the record either way.
a_caveat_on_my_own_gate: C66's cascade predicate passed a crossed-pair gate at 0.018% against 0.051%. This result shows crossed-pair rates overstate real risk, which makes C66's margin MORE comfortable rather than less -- but it also means a crossed-pair gate is a conservative screen, not a measurement of actual false matches. The stronger test is the one run here: tighten and count how many real matched rows depend on the looseness.
does_not_reach_a_pass: no code changed; unattributed stays at 255
